mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over two consecutive months signals a tightening cycle, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises by >0.25% in two consecutive monthly releases
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the unemployment rate below 4% for three consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which increases wage pressures and inflation expectations, ultimately reducing equity valuations and producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.3%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL above their respective 12-month moving averages signals a monetary policy tightening coinciding with accelerating inflation, which increases real interest rates and depresses equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 12-mo MA and CPIAUCSL > 12-mo MA in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.6%) in at least 55% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent monthly decline in both real personal income (proxied by HOUST) and personal consumption expenditures (proxied by RSAFS) by more than 0.5% signals deteriorating household demand, which reduces corporate sales and earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST and RSAFS both decline by >0.5% in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 35% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in payroll employment (PAYEMS) of more than 1% month-over-month for three consecutive months signals robust labor market expansion, which supports earnings growth and positive equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS monthly change > 1% for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of at least 0.5% for four consecutive months signals a manufacturing expansion, which boosts corporate revenues and profit margins, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO monthly change >= 0.5% for four consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.4%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.
